brief_data.deck: Eos Energy Enterprises, the Nasdaq-listed maker of American-made zinc-based batteries for three-to-twelve-hour grid storage, appointed Michelle Buczkowski Chief Commercial Officer on 24 August 2026 with sales, marketing and communications reporting to her, and carries a record $807M backlog into its factory consolidation.

risks.label: CAPACITY
risks.detail: Loss-making with the 2026 guidance cut in August and the shares far below their 52-week high; discretionary spend is under pressure.
risks.counter: Associate-level entry at $1-2M a year with a margin-linked review; the ask is small on purpose.

risks.label: NO CAPITAL EVENT
risks.detail: The trigger is a reorganisation of the commercial function, not new money.
risks.counter: The reorganisation puts marketing under one new owner, which is exactly who buys a sponsorship.

risks.label: PRODUCT OFF-CAMERA
risks.detail: Grid-scale batteries have no role in the race car or the race weekend.
risks.counter: A trackside storage showcase and the American-made story give the product a place to be seen.

extended.ask: A 25-minute call with Michelle Buczkowski before 20 October to test whether an associate-level, three-year Formula E entry on Andretti fits the 2027 commercial plan, and to confirm the budget capacity the balance sheet allows.

value.text: American-made electric storage on the American team in Formula E's first Gen4 season: a home-market story for Austin and Miami and a clean fit with the championship's energy narrative.
value.label: Brand story

value.text: Utilities, independent power producers and data-centre developers are the buyers of long-duration storage; the Austin and Miami paddocks are a place to host them in the launch year.
value.label: Customer hospitality

value.text: A storage showcase built from the company's own cubes at the US rounds, branded as the team's energy partner, gives the product a visible place at the event without claiming a role in the car.
value.label: Trackside showcase

value.text: Official Energy Storage Partner designation at associate level, rear-wing placement, Austin and Miami hospitality, and content on the American energy transition for the partner's channels.
value.label: What the team gives back

why_now.text: On 24 August 2026 Eos appointed Michelle Buczkowski Chief Commercial Officer, moving her from Chief Administration Officer; sales, business development, government affairs, marketing and communications now report to her, and she owns the path from first customer engagement through order intake and revenue. The previous commercial chief, Nathan Kroeker, leaves on 20 October after a transition.
why_now.label: Trigger

why_now.text: Marketing and communications moving under a single new commercial owner is the moment a company decides how it wants to be seen. The 2027 plan is being written in the transition window, and a sponsorship proposal that arrives before 20 October lands on a desk that is still being set up.
why_now.label: Why a reorganisation counts

why_now.text: Second-quarter revenue of $68.8M was up 351% on 207% more cube deliveries, backlog reached a record $807M, and 2026 guidance is $300M-$350M. The company is loss-making, with a $275.7M net loss in the quarter, and is consolidating manufacturing; a $303.5M DOE-guaranteed loan funds expansion to 8 GWh by 2027.
why_now.label: The business behind it

why_now.text: Season 13 opens with the Jeddah E-Prix on 18-19 December 2026; the Austin E-Prix on 6 February and the Miami E-Prix on 20 February 2027 are the American rounds, and both fall inside a first season's activation plan.
why_now.label: Calendar window

why_team.text: Andretti Formula E is owned by TWG Motorsports, runs Nissan powertrains from Season 13, and carries TWG AI, Quest Global, Crowe UK and Reflo as partners. There is no energy or storage brand on the car, so the lane is open in the sponsor table.
why_team.label: The American team

why_team.text: An American-made storage company on the American team has a natural stage at Austin and Miami in February 2027, where its utility and developer customers can be hosted.
why_team.label: Home rounds

why_team.text: Envision Racing would look like the storage team, but its parent Envision Group is itself a renewables and clean-technology group; a competing storage brand does not sit on that car.
why_team.label: Why not the obvious alternative

why_team.text: This is a MODE B case: grid-scale batteries stay off the race car. What Andretti gets is an American energy story for the Gen4 era and a partner whose product can be shown at the track, not used in it.
why_team.label: Honest fit

ruled_out.reason: Envision Group, the team's parent, is a renewables and clean-technology group: a category conflict for a storage brand. Paysafe takes title from Season 13.

ruled_out.reason: TotalEnergies holds the energy lane; the electronics roster (Mouser, TTI, Molex, KYOCERA AVX) fills the technical side.
Castrol in the energy lane; a British story with no US angle.

ruled_out.reason: German works teams; no American story.

brief_data.bottom_line: A public, $300M-revenue American storage maker that has just put its whole commercial path under one new owner: a real trigger, a thin balance sheet, and an open lane on the American Formula E team with two US rounds in February. WARM at 62 because capacity, not fit, holds it back.

brief_data.the_case_p1: Eos, headquartered in Edison, New Jersey, makes Znyth aqueous-zinc and Z3 zinc-bromine batteries in Pennsylvania for three-to-twelve-hour storage. Second-quarter revenue was $68.8M, up 351% on 207% more cube deliveries; backlog rose 25% in the quarter to a record $807M; full-year guidance was tightened to $300M-$350M. The company is loss-making: the quarter's net loss was $275.7M and the gross loss $48.8M. A $303.5M loan guaranteed by the US Department of Energy, closed in December 2024, funds expansion to 8 GWh of capacity by 2027, and Cerberus is a strategic investor.
brief_data.the_case_p2: The trigger is a person, not a round. On 24 August the company put its Chief Administration Officer in charge of the whole commercial path, from first customer engagement to revenue, and moved marketing and communications under her; the previous commercial chief leaves on 20 October. A company that has just centralised its market voice, with shareholders watching the price fall, has a reason to be seen. Formula E is the electric stage that fits.

brief_data.why_team_para: Andretti Formula E is the American team on the grid, owned by TWG Motorsports, running Nissan powertrains from Season 13 with TWG AI, Quest Global, Crowe UK and Reflo as partners and no energy or storage brand on the car. An American-made storage company on the American team gives both a home story at Austin and Miami, and the energy lane is open in the sponsor table. Envision, the other natural fit, is ruled out by its parent's own energy business.
brief_data.deal_arch_para: Entry as Official Energy Storage Partner at associate level. <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9.5'>THREE YEARS</font>, Seasons 13-15, sized to the balance sheet: estimated $1-2M a year with a review clause tied to the company's gross-margin turn. Scope: rear-wing placement, Austin and Miami hospitality for utility and developer customers, and a trackside storage showcase built from the company's own cubes.
brief_data.why_now_callout: <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9'>WHY NOW</font>  The new Chief Commercial Officer owns marketing from 24 August and the transition completes on 20 October; the 2027 plan is being written now. Season 13 opens with the Jeddah E-Prix on 18-19 December, and the Austin E-Prix on 6 February and the Miami E-Prix on 20 February 2027 are the American rounds.
brief_data.decision_maker_bio: Buczkowski became Chief Commercial Officer on 24 August 2026, moving from Chief Administration Officer; sales, business development, government affairs, marketing and communications report to her. Path: Joe Mastrangelo, CEO since 2019; Eric Javidi, CFO. No chief marketing officer is listed; marketing sits under her.
brief_data.decision_maker_role: Chief Commercial Officer, Eos Energy Enterprises
brief_data.opening_angle_quote: “Michelle, marketing now reports to you, and Formula E's American rounds land in Austin and Miami in February. Andretti is the American team with no storage partner. 25 minutes to see whether a small three-year entry belongs in your 2027 plan?”
